news.headline: Bihar likely to present over ₹10,000 cr demand to Centre to compensate flood damages
news.story_lead: Bihar likely to present over ₹10,000 cr demand to Centre to compensate flood damages The first wave of flooding struck in the opening week of September, affecting over 50 lakh people across more than 2,000 villages in 15 districts of Bihar. The Bihar government is preparing to place a demand of more than ₹ 10,000 crore before the Centre as compensation for the widespread damage caused by the recent floods to people, agriculture, and public infrastructure, a senior officer familiar with the assessment process said on Friday. The first wave of flooding struck in the opening week of September, setting multiple highest flood levels (HFL) and affecting over 50 lakh people across more than 2,000 villages in 576 panchayats of 15 districts by the first week of October.
news.full_article_text: Bihar likely to present over ₹10,000 cr demand to Centre to compensate flood damages The first wave of flooding struck in the opening week of September, affecting over 50 lakh people across more than 2,000 villages in 15 districts of Bihar. The Bihar government is preparing to place a demand of more than ₹ 10,000 crore before the Centre as compensation for the widespread damage caused by the recent floods to people, agriculture, and public infrastructure, a senior officer familiar with the assessment process said on Friday. The first wave of flooding struck in the opening week of September, setting multiple highest flood levels (HFL) and affecting over 50 lakh people across more than 2,000 villages in 576 panchayats of 15 districts by the first week of October. “The assessment of damages is in the final stages. We hope that the assessment will conclude next week and the final demand will be sent to the Centre soon after,” a principal secretary-rank officer said. A senior official of the disaster management department (DMD), the nodal agency, said the process was delayed by a second wave that hit the north-western districts late and caused extensive damage to standing crops, infrastructure, school buildings, embankments and roads. “Final assessment is waiting for the receding of water from the fields,” he added. The assessment The agriculture department’s preliminary assessment has put crop losses at around ₹ 270 crore, covering roughly 1.7 lakh hectares across more than 100 blocks in 18 districts, with paddy, maize, vegetables and banana crops among the worst hit. Officials indicated the figure could rise further once water fully recedes and detailed field verification is completed; some estimates already point to losses exceeding ₹ 300 crore. Under NDRF norms, eligible farmers stand to receive input subsidies ranging from ₹ 8,500 per hectare for unirrigated land to ₹ 17,000 per hectare for irrigated land, and up to ₹ 22,500 per hectare for perennial crops. Major infrastructure devastation has been reported by the rural works department (RWD), water resources department (WRD), road construction department (RCD) and the education department. Over 4,000 government schools were submerged across the flood-hit districts, disrupting education for more than three lakh students; many buildings suffered severe structural damage, and some collapsed. Roads, embankments and rural connectivity infrastructure have also taken a heavy toll. "Rural roads have been damaged extensively, and it might take over ₹ 3,000 crore to restore them. Major district roads and state highways have also borne a heavy brunt of the floods," said the officer. The DMD has so far transferred ₹ 579.23 crore as immediate ex-gratia assistance of ₹ 7,000 per family to 8,27,472 verified flood-affected households through direct benefit transfer. Community kitchens numbering over 1,200 have served more than 1.2 crore meals, while relief camps, dry ration packets, polythene sheets and cattle feed have been distributed on a large scale. The overall expenditure on compensation, relief measures, and community kitchens is estimated at around ₹ 2,000 crore, though the final consolidated figure is still being compiled. A senior engineer of the WRD said that embankments on the river Gandak have been damaged at multiple locations. “As the river has set new HFLs, embankments are required to be further strengthened with technical modification. The state has been facing floods due to the discharge in rivers originating from Nepal,” said the engineer, adding that an estimate for embankment reconstruction is also being prepared. Union minister's assurance A Central team led by Union agriculture and rural development minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan visited various flood-affected areas on 16 September, along with chief minister Samrat Choudhary. The Union minister conducted aerial surveys and ground inspections in districts including Patna, Saran, Vaishali, Munger and Bhagalpur, travelling by boat and tractor through inundated villages. He described the floods as among the most severe in years, with water levels exceeding those of 2016 in some areas, and assured full cooperation from the Centre to mitigate people's suffering and restore damaged infrastructure. Opposition's pressure Opposition leaders also stepped up pressure on both the Centre and the state government. Leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, has criticised the BJP-led “double-engine” governments for failing to deliver a permanent solution to Bihar’s annual flood crisis, asking what concrete change has been achieved on the ground in the last 17 years. He has called for lasting measures rather than repeated cycles of relief and assurances. Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and opposition leader in the state assembly, Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, also accused the Centre of stepmotherly treatment, demanded that the floods be declared a national disaster, and sought substantially higher financial assistance for affected families and farmers. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Subhash Pathak Subhash Pathak is special correspondent of Hindustan Times with over 15 years of experience in journalism, covering issues related to governance, legislature, police, Maoism, urban and road infrastructure of Bihar and Jharkhand. news.full_article_text: Parl panel seeks public tech strategy, new coordination body New Delhi: The Parliamentary Committee on External Affairs has asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to prepare a public “technology vision and strategy document”, saying it was surprised that India lacks a single written strategy linking technology with its foreign policy New Delhi: The Parliamentary Committee on External Affairs has asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to prepare a public “technology vision and strategy document”, saying it was surprised that India lacks a single written strategy linking technology with its foreign policy. Calling the current approach “fragmentary, piecemeal and ad hoc”, the panel said individual successes cannot substitute for a national vision. The committee, chaired by Shashi Tharoor, recommended that the MEA work with the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and other departments to prepare the document after consulting academia, research institutions and industry. The panel said the document should outline India’s goals, priorities and the roles of different ministries. It also recommended a separate “technology diplomacy strategy” for the MEA. Both documents should be made public and reviewed periodically, it said. The committee called for a formal inter-ministerial body on technology diplomacy, chaired by the MEA and including the IT, science, space and commerce ministries, to ensure regular coordination rather than a case-by-case approach. The recommendations are part of the committee’s 17th report, adopted on September 22 and presented to the Lok Sabha Speaker on September 25. Revision of AI strategy The report said India had significant strengths in artificial intelligence (AI) but continued to face gaps in computing power, data centre capacity, access to advanced chips and private investment in large AI models. It noted that NITI Aayog’s national AI strategy was drafted before the emergence of large language models and recommended that NITI Aayog and MeitY revise it in consultation with the MEA. India has risen to third place from seventh globally on the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Tool, an interactive benchmarking suite developed by the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) to compare national AI ecosystems. However, the committee cautioned that the gap with the US and China remained substantial, calling it “a difference of kind and not only of degree”. The recommendations come as MeitY announced on Thursday that it would release a consultation paper within a month as a precursor to framing AI regulations. The paper will focus on safety, humanity, skilling, inclusivity and harm mitigation. Data centre figures unverified The committee questioned claims that India holds about 20% of the world’s data but accounts for only 3% of global data centre capacity. MeitY told the panel that neither figure was officially verified. Industry estimates, cited in the report, suggest capacity may need to rise from around 1.5 gigawatts in 2025 to 5-10 GW by 2030. The committee recommended that the MEA coordinate with MeitY and other ministries to collect and publish verified data to guide international investments and technology partnerships. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sejal Sharma I am a technology policy reporter with the National Political Bureau at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi. I cover digital policy and the intersection of technology and society, focusing mainly on what's happening in India. My beat often involves tracking platform regulation, privacy, internet curbs, and the real-world impact of digital rules, among other things. Can usually be found reading government notifications so that you don't have to. I cover three key ministries: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Ministry of Communications, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B). I am originally from New Delhi and a graduate of the Asian College of Journalism, Chennai. Over the past nine years, I have worked across television, digital and print media with The Secretariat, CNN-News18, Tiranga TV, Interesting Engineering, and now Hindustan Times. New Delhi: The Parliamentary Committee on External Affairs has asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to prepare a public “technology vision and strategy document”, saying it was surprised that India lacks a single written strategy linking technology with its foreign policy. Calling the current approach “fragmentary, piecemeal and ad hoc”, the panel said individual successes cannot substitute for a national vision.

The committee, chaired by Shashi Tharoor, recommended that the MEA work with the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and other departments to prepare the document after consulting academia, research institutions and industry.

The panel said the document should outline India’s goals, priorities and the roles of different ministries. It also recommended a separate “technology diplomacy strategy” for the MEA. Both documents should be made public and reviewed periodically, it said.

The committee called for a formal inter-ministerial body on technology diplomacy, chaired by the MEA and including the IT, science, space and commerce ministries, to ensure regular coordination rather than a case-by-case approach.
The recommendations are part of the committee’s 17th report, adopted on September 22 and presented to the Lok Sabha Speaker on September 25.

The report said India had significant strengths in artificial intelligence (AI) but continued to face gaps in computing power, data centre capacity, access to advanced chips and private investment in large AI models. It noted that NITI Aayog’s national AI strategy was drafted before the emergence of large language models and recommended that NITI Aayog and MeitY revise it in consultation with the MEA.

news.headline: Telangana ACB arrests civil supplies manager over ₹9.41 crore disproportionate assets
news.story_lead: Telangana ACB arrests civil supplies manager over ₹9.41 crore disproportionate assets Telangana ACB arrested civil supplies manager Vasamsetti Narasimha Rao over alleged disproportionate assets of ₹ 9.41 crore, with market value estimated above ₹ 40 crore. The Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Saturday arrested a state civil supplies department assistant manager for allegedly amassing assets worth ₹ 9.41 crore disproportionate to his known sources of income, with their market value estimated at over ₹ 40 crore, officials said. An official statement from ACB director general Charu Sinha said that ACB teams on Friday conducted searches at seven places linked to Vasamsetti Narasimha Rao, who is working as an assistant manager (technical) in the state civil supplies department and currently serving as district manager in Mahabubabad district.
news.full_article_text: Telangana ACB arrests civil supplies manager over ₹9.41 crore disproportionate assets Telangana ACB arrested civil supplies manager Vasamsetti Narasimha Rao over alleged disproportionate assets of ₹ 9.41 crore, with market value estimated above ₹ 40 crore. The Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Saturday arrested a state civil supplies department assistant manager for allegedly amassing assets worth ₹ 9.41 crore disproportionate to his known sources of income, with their market value estimated at over ₹ 40 crore, officials said. An official statement from ACB director general Charu Sinha said that ACB teams on Friday conducted searches at seven places linked to Vasamsetti Narasimha Rao, who is working as an assistant manager (technical) in the state civil supplies department and currently serving as district manager in Mahabubabad district. “The searches went on till late in the evening. Searches are also being conducted in the properties belonging to the suspected benamis of Narasimha Rao. As per the market value, the assets belonging to him and that of his benamis together are worth nearly ₹ 100 crore,” a senior official of the ACB privy to the information said. The case was registered under relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act. Investigators identified several residential buildings, agricultural lands, open plots, vehicles, gold and silver ornaments, and other valuables during the searches. According to ACB officials, five open plots measuring a total of 1,230.16 square yards were identified at Ballepalli, Raghunathapalem and Velugumatla in Khammam district. The properties, registered in the names of Narasimha Rao and his wife, have a combined registration value of ₹ 30.72 lakh. The bureau also identified agricultural lands in Suryapet district, including approximately 1.08 acres at Kalmala Chervu, 21.3 acres at Sirikonda and two parcels measuring 5.31 acres each at Namavaram in Mothe mandal. While the combined registration value of these agricultural properties was recorded at approximately ₹ 1.17 crore, the ACB found that the agreement values of certain properties were substantially higher. In particular, the 21.3-acre agricultural property at Sirikonda had a registered value of ₹ 76 lakh, whereas its agreement value was ₹ 6.54 crore. Similarly, each of the two agricultural properties at Namavaram had a registered value of ₹ 19.25 lakh against an agreement value of ₹ 1.92 crore. Investigators also identified three residential properties, including a ground-plus-two-storey RCC building and a ground-plus-four-storey RCC building at Kaviraj Nagar in Khammam, besides a three-storey residential property at Sagar Enclave in Bairamalguda, LB Nagar, Hyderabad. These buildings, standing in the names of the official, his wife and his father-in-law, have a combined documented value of ₹ 1.58 crore. Among the movable assets identified were a Hyundai Creta car valued at ₹ 18.49 lakh, a TVS Jupiter scooter worth ₹ 1.05 lakh and a Honda Activa scooter valued at ₹ 50,000. The ACB also identified household articles valued at ₹ 33.48 lakh, besides approximately 360.97 grams of gold and 331.58 grams of silver ornaments with a combined estimated value of ₹ 9.39 lakh. Cash amounting to ₹ 15,600 was seized from the official’s residence. The bureau stated that the total value of assets identified so far was approximately ₹ 9.41 crore, based on its property statement. It said the prevailing market value of the immovable properties could be substantially higher than their recorded registration values. The ACB is also investigating allegations that Rao acquired a rice mill in the name of another person as benami property. “We are verifying the ownership of the suspected benami asset, the source of investment and the financial transactions involved in its acquisition,” Charu Sinha said. Officials are also examining his bank accounts and lockers to determine whether he holds additional assets. Transactions linked to certain businesses have also come under scrutiny. The agency is expected to establish the extent of the alleged disproportionate assets after completing the searches and examining the financial records and property documents. The ACB director general said further investigation was underway to establish the actual ownership of the identified properties, their sources of acquisition and the funds used to purchase them. Rao joined the civil supplies department as a technical assistant in 2011 and subsequently worked in Khammam and Nirmal before taking up his present responsibilities in Mahabubabad. The ACB said its preliminary findings indicated that he had allegedly accumulated assets disproportionate to his known sources of income during his 15 years in service. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Srinivasa Rao Apparasu Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana . He has over three decades of reporting experience.

The Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Saturday arrested a state civil supplies department assistant manager for allegedly amassing assets worth ₹ 9.41 crore disproportionate to his known sources of income, with their market value estimated at over ₹ 40 crore, officials said.

An official statement from ACB director general Charu Sinha said that ACB teams on Friday conducted searches at seven places linked to Vasamsetti Narasimha Rao, who is working as an assistant manager (technical) in the state civil supplies department and currently serving as district manager in Mahabubabad district.

“The searches went on till late in the evening. Searches are also being conducted in the properties belonging to the suspected benamis of Narasimha Rao. As per the market value, the assets belonging to him and that of his benamis together are worth nearly ₹ 100 crore,” a senior official of the ACB privy to the information said.
The case was registered under relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

news.headline: ED Arrests Sadhna Group Chairman Rakesh Kumar Gupta in Insolvency-Linked Money Laundering Case
news.story_lead: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Rakesh Kumar Gupta, Chairman of Delhi-based Sadhna Group, in connection with a money laundering probe into alleged irregularities under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The agency alleges that Gupta manipulated insolvency proceedings to settle ₹110.10 crore in Income Tax liabilities for just ₹20 lakh, generating overall proceeds of crime valued at ₹168 crore.
news.full_article_text:
### Enforcement Directorate Action
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Rakesh Kumar Gupta, the 63-year-old Chairman of Delhi-based media and broadcast company Sadhna Group, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). Gupta was taken into custody in Delhi and produced before Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler at a Ghaziabad camp office, where he was remanded to five days of ED custody.

### Primary Allegations and Financial Irregularities
The money laundering investigation originates from a September FIR registered by the Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the Delhi Police. Key allegations detailed in the case include:
- **Insolvency Process Manipulation:** Gupta allegedly engineered the insolvency of Sadhna Media Pvt. Ltd. (SMPL) by controlling 99.41% of the Committee of Creditors (CoC) through related entities. Through this setup, Income Tax department dues of ₹110.10 crore were settled for a nominal sum of ₹20 lakh.
- **Diversion to Connected Creditors:** Under Gupta's influence, SMPL paid ₹4.48 crore to connected creditors, which included ₹2.99 crore transferred to his own firm, Sharpline Broadcast.
- **Cryptocurrency and Hawala Channels:** The accused allegedly received over ₹2 crore in cash through hawala and cryptocurrency transactions during the resale of SMPL/Aryan TV.
- **SEBI Findings:** In May 2025, SEBI identified Gupta as the primary mastermind in the share price manipulation of Sadhna Broadcast, holding him jointly and severally liable for roughly ₹58 crore.
- **Total Proceeds of Crime:** The ED informed the court that total proceeds of crime in this case stand at ₹168 crore.

### Judicial Ruling and Arguments
Defence counsel contended that neither the Income Tax Department nor SEBI had filed a criminal complaint against Gupta, pointing out that he obtained a no-dues certificate from tax authorities and paid the SEBI penalty. However, the court rejected these arguments, stating that an ED investigation under PMLA remains legally valid even in the absence of explicit complaints from those departments. The court noted that a loss exceeding ₹100 crore to the public exchequer warrants a thorough probe, especially since the money trail involves non-banking channels and unexamined digital evidence.

news.mains_notes:
### Corporate Insolvency & Financial Governance Concerns
1. **CoC Manipulation:** The presence of related creditors holding dominant stakes (e.g., 99.41%) in a Committee of Creditors can lead to collusive resolution plans that undervalue legitimate public claims such as tax liabilities.
2. **Money Laundering Dynamics:** Integration of non-banking channels (hawala, crypto) alongside legal insolvency processes creates complex money laundering networks.
3. **Regulatory Synergy:** PMLA provisions can be independently invoked to target proceeds of crime even when underlying statutory bodies have not initiated separate criminal complaints.

hindi_translation.headline: ईडी ने इंसॉल्वेंसी से जुड़े मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग मामले में साधना ग्रुप के चेयरमैन राकेश कुमार गुप्ता को गिरफ्तार किया
hindi_translation.story_lead: प्रवर्तन निदेशालय (ईडी) ने दिल्ली स्थित साधना ग्रुप के चेयरमैन राकेश कुमार गुप्ता को इंसॉल्वेंसी एंड बैंकरप्सी कोड (आईबीसी) प्रक्रियाओं में गड़बड़ी से जुड़े मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग मामले में गिरफ्तार किया है। आरोप है कि गुप्ता ने दिवाला प्रक्रिया में हेरफेर कर ₹110.10 करोड़ के आयकर बकाए को केवल ₹20 लाख में निपटा दिया, जिससे कुल ₹168 करोड़ का अपराध जनित धन (Proceeds of Crime) उत्पन्न हुआ।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### प्रवर्तन निदेशालय की कार्रवाई
प्रवर्तन निदेशालय (ईडी) ने धन शोधन निवारण अधिनियम (PMLA) के तहत दिल्ली स्थित मीडिया कंपनी साधना ग्रुप के 63 वर्षीय चेयरमैन राकेश कुमार गुप्ता को गिरफ्तार किया है। गुप्ता को दिल्ली में हिरासत में लिया गया और गाजियाबाद स्थित अतिरिक्त सत्र न्यायाधीश सौरभ प्रताप सिंह लालर के आवासीय शिविर कार्यालय में पेश किया गया, जहां से उन्हें 5 दिन की ईडी हिरासत में भेज दिया गया।

### मुख्य आरोप और वित्तीय अनियमितताएं
मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग का यह मामला दिल्ली पुलिस की आर्थिक अपराध शाखा (EOW) द्वारा सितंबर में दर्ज प्राथमिकी से शुरू हुआ है। मामले में दर्ज मुख्य आरोप निम्नलिखित हैं:
- **दिवाला प्रक्रिया में हेरफेर:** गुप्ता पर आरोप है कि उन्होंने संबंधित देनदारों के जरिए साधना मीडिया प्राइवेट लिमिटेड (SMPL) की लेनदारों की समिति (CoC) में 99.41% नियंत्रण हासिल कर कंपनी को दिवालिया बनाया। इस व्यवस्था के माध्यम से ₹110.10 करोड़ के आयकर बकाए को महज ₹20 लाख में निपटा दिया गया।
- **संबंधित देनदारों को राशि हस्तांतरण:** एसएमपीएल से जुड़े देनदारों को ₹4.48 करोड़ का भुगतान कराया गया, जिसमें गुप्ता की अपनी कंपनी शारपलाइन ब्रॉडकास्ट को दिया गया ₹2.99 करोड़ का भुगतान भी शामिल है।
- **क्रिप्टो और हवाला माध्यम:** एसएमपीएल/आर्यन टीवी की पुनर्विक्री पर क्रिप्टो-करेंसी और हवाला के जरिए ₹2 करोड़ से अधिक की नकदी प्राप्त करने का आरोप है।
- **सेबी के निष्कर्ष:** मई 2025 में सेबी ने गुप्ता को साधना ब्रॉडकास्ट के शेयर मूल्य हेरफेर का 'मास्टरमाइंड' करार दिया था और उन्हें लगभग ₹58 करोड़ के लिए उत्तरदायी ठहराया था।
- **कुल अपराध जनित धन:** ईडी ने अदालत को बताया कि इस मामले में कुल अपराध जनित धन ₹168 करोड़ है।

### अदालती कार्यवाही एवं आदेश
बचाव पक्ष के वकील ने तर्क दिया कि सेबी या आयकर विभाग ने गुप्ता के खिलाफ कोई शिकायत नहीं दर्ज की थी, उन्हें कर विभाग से नो-ड्यूज प्रमाणपत्र मिला हुआ है और सेबी जुर्माना भर दिया गया है। हालांकि, अदालत ने इन तर्कों को खारिज करते हुए कहा कि केवल शिकायत न होने के आधार पर ईडी की जांच को अवैध नहीं माना जा सकता। अदालत ने कहा कि सरकारी खजाने को ₹100 करोड़ से अधिक का नुकसान हुआ है, जिसकी गहन जांच आवश्यक है।

news.headline: CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke and Key Leaders Detained at Delhi Airport Ahead of Planned Demonstration
news.story_lead: Delhi Police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke along with co-convener Saurav Das and spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka upon their landing at the Delhi airport from Mumbai on October 10, 2026. The political pressure group leaders were arriving in the national capital to organize a protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral roll revision irregularities.
news.full_article_text:
Three prominent figures of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)—founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convener Saurav Das, and spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka—were taken into police custody immediately after their flight from Mumbai touched down at the Delhi airport on Saturday morning, October 10, 2026.

The CJP leadership had traveled to Delhi to lead a proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The group sought the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process carried out for electoral rolls. Dipke had previously announced his travel plans to Delhi via social media platforms.

According to senior police officials, personnel from the Southwest district police were stationed at the airport after receiving special access passes to enter the restricted premises. The police operation was designed to intercept and detain arriving CJP leaders and supporters coming in from various states.

Police authorities declined to disclose the specific facility or location where the detained leaders were moved, citing security protocols. In response, the CJP issued an official statement strongly condemning the action, characterizing it as an authoritarian attempt by law enforcement to suppress peaceful demonstrations and restrict fundamental freedom of movement.

The CJP condemned the preventive detention, alleging a violation of freedom of movement.

hindi_translation.headline: दिल्ली हवाई अड्डे पर कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके और प्रमुख नेता हिरासत में लिए गए
hindi_translation.story_lead: दिल्ली पुलिस ने 10 अक्टूबर 2026 को मुंबई से दिल्ली हवाई अड्डे पहुंचे कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) के संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके, सह-संयोजक सौरव दास और प्रवक्ता आशुतोष रांका को हिरासत में ले लिया। ये नेता जंतर-मंतर पर मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर प्रदर्शन करने आ रहे थे।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) के तीन प्रमुख नेताओं—संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके, सह-संयोजक सौरव दास और प्रवक्ता आशुतोष रांका—को शनिवार सुबह, 10 अक्टूबर 2026 को मुंबई से आई उनकी उड़ान के उतरते ही दिल्ली पुलिस ने हिरासत में ले लिया।

CJP नेतृत्व मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) प्रक्रिया में कथित अनियमितताओं के विरोध में मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर जंतर-मंतर पर एक प्रस्तावित विरोध प्रदर्शन में भाग लेने दिल्ली आया था। दीपके ने पहले ही सोशल मीडिया के माध्यम से दिल्ली आने की घोषणा की थी।

वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधिकारियों के अनुसार, दक्षिण-पश्चिम जिला पुलिस के कर्मियों को विशेष पास जारी कर हवाई अड्डे के भीतर तैनात किया गया था। इस अभियान का उद्देश्य विभिन्न राज्यों से आने वाले CJP नेताओं और समर्थकों को रोकना था।

सुरक्षा कारणों का हवाला देते हुए पुलिस अधिकारियों ने उस स्थान का खुलासा करने से इनकार कर दिया जहां हिरासत में लिए गए नेताओं को ले जाया गया। जवाब में, CJP ने एक बयान जारी कर इस कार्रवाई की कड़ी निंदा की और इसे शांतिपूर्ण प्रदर्शनों को दबाने तथा आवाजाही की स्वतंत्रता का उल्लंघन बताया।
bullet_points: CJP संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके, सह-संयोजक सौरव दास और प्रवक्ता आशुतोष रांका दिल्ली हवाई अड्डे पर हिरासत में लिए गए।
नेता 10 अक्टूबर 2026 की सुबह मुंबई से दिल्ली पहुंचे थे।
प्रस्तावित विरोध प्रदर्शन नई दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर आयोजित होना था।
प्रदर्शनकारी मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग कर रहे थे।
मुख्य मुद्दा मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) में कथित अनियमितताएं थीं।
दक्षिण-पश्चिम जिला पुलिस ने विशेष पास का उपयोग कर हवाई अड्डे पर इस कार्रवाई को अंजाम दिया।
सुरक्षा कारणों से पुलिस ने नेताओं के वर्तमान स्थान का खुलासा नहीं किया।
CJP ने निरोधक कार्रवाई की निंदा करते हुए इसे आवाजाही की स्वतंत्रता का उल्लंघन करार दिया।
key_facts: हिरासत में लिए गए व्यक्ति: अभिजीत दीपके (संस्थापक), सौरव दास (सह-संयोजक), आशुतोष रांका (प्रवक्ता)।
संगठन: कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP)।
निशाने पर अधिकारी: मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार।
संबंधित प्रक्रिया: मतदाता सूची का विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR)।
कार्रवाई करने वाली एजेंसी: दिल्ली पुलिस (दक्षिण-पश्चिम जिला पुलिस)।
घटना का स्थान: दिल्ली हवाई अड्डा (मुंबई से आगमन पर)।

news.headline: Asian Games Medalist Murali Sreeshankar Criticizes Kerala Government Over Lack of Outreach
news.story_lead: Indian long jumper and Asian Games silver medalist Murali Sreeshankar expressed discontent over the lack of communication and recognition from Kerala's top leadership. He revealed that neither the state's Chief Minister nor the Sports Minister contacted him, whereas he received encouragement and offers from Tamil Nadu.
news.full_article_text:
### Sports Administrative Concerns: Sreeshankar Highlights Lack of Support

• **Discontent Over Absence of Outreach:** Asian Games silver medalist long jumper Murali Sreeshankar publicly criticized the Kerala state government, stating that neither Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan nor the state Sports Minister had reached out to extend congratulations or offer administrative backing.
• **Offers from Neighboring State:** Sreeshankar revealed that while support from his home state was lacking, he had received administrative and sporting offers from Tamil Nadu.
• **Highlighting Sports Governance Issues:** The public comments by the elite athlete draw attention to broader systemic challenges regarding athlete welfare, timely state patronage, and the lack of structured communication between state authorities and top-tier sportspersons in India.
bullet_points: Asian Games silver medalist long jumper Murali Sreeshankar publicly criticized the Kerala state government.
He stated that neither Kerala's Chief Minister nor the Sports Minister had contacted him to acknowledge his international achievements.
Sreeshankar revealed receiving administrative and sporting offers from Tamil Nadu.
The issue underlines gaps in state-level athlete welfare, support mechanisms, and official recognition.
Differences in state sports policies often lead to discussions on athlete recruitment and inter-state migration.
key_facts: Murali Sreeshankar is an Asian Games silver medalist in long jump.
He publicly reported receiving no contact from Kerala's Chief Minister or Sports Minister.
He confirmed receiving sports-related offers from the state of Tamil Nadu.
exam_relevance: Prelims: General awareness regarding prominent Indian sports personalities and Asian Games medalists.
Mains: General Studies Paper II (Governance and Public Policy - Sports Governance) and athlete welfare policies in India.
news.upsc_analysis: The issue highlights administrative inertia in state sports departments and the necessity for robust, institutionalized state patronage for elite athletes to prevent talent migration and ensure sustained sporting performance.
causes: Lack of direct communication or formal outreach from Kerala state leaders to the medalist.
impacts: Potential migration of top athletic talent to states offering better incentives and proactive administrative support.
Increased public debate over Kerala's sports governance and athlete recognition policies.
challenges: Ensuring timely, non-bureaucratic recognition and incentive disbursement for elite national athletes.
Disparities in support and welfare policies among different Indian states.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India (State List - Entry 33: Sports, Entertainment and Amusements).
way_forward: Implement uniform, automated reward and welfare frameworks for international medalists to eliminate bureaucratic delays and ensure prompt state recognition.
news.mains_notes: State patronage is crucial for sustaining elite athletic careers in India. Disparities in state-level policies and administrative delays often prompt top athletes to seek financial and infrastructure support from other states.
mains_questions: Analyze the structural challenges in state-level sports governance in India. How can standardized policies prevent athlete migration across states?

hindi_translation.headline: एशियाई खेलों के पदक विजेता मुरली श्रीशंकर ने केरल सरकार द्वारा उपेक्षा पर जताई नाराजगी
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय लंबी कूद एथलीट और एशियाई खेलों के रजत पदक विजेता मुरली श्रीशंकर ने केरल के शीर्ष नेतृत्व से संपर्क और मान्यता न मिलने पर असंतोष व्यक्त किया। उन्होंने बताया कि राज्य के मुख्यमंत्री या खेल मंत्री में से किसी ने भी उनसे संपर्क नहीं किया, जबकि उन्हें तमिलनाडु से प्रस्ताव मिले थे।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### खेल प्रशासनिक चिंताएं: श्रीशंकर ने सरकारी सहायता की कमी पर उठाया सवाल

• **संपर्क न होने पर असंतोष:** एशियाई खेलों के रजत पदक विजेता एथलीट मुरली श्रीशंकर ने केरल राज्य सरकार की आलोचना करते हुए कहा कि मुख्यमंत्री पिनराई विजयन या राज्य के खेल मंत्री में से किसी ने भी उनसे संपर्क कर बधाई नहीं दी और न ही सहायता का आश्वासन दिया।
• **पड़ोसी राज्य से ऑफर:** श्रीशंकर ने खुलासा किया कि उनके गृह राज्य केरल से समर्थन की कमी के बीच उन्हें तमिलनाडु से खेल और प्रशासनिक प्रस्ताव प्राप्त हुए हैं।
• **खेल प्रशासन के मुद्दे:** शीर्ष एथलीट के इन बयानों से भारत में एथलीटों के कल्याण, समय पर राज्य सहायता, और खेल प्रशासकों तथा अंतरराष्ट्रीय खिलाड़ियों के बीच संवाद की कमी जैसे मुद्दों पर ध्यान केंद्रित हुआ है।

उन्होंने कहा कि मुख्यमंत्री और खेल मंत्री में से किसी ने भी उनकी सफलताओं पर उनसे संपर्क नहीं किया।

news.exam_corner_topic: Protest Against Chief Election Commissioner and Public Order Measures
static_gk: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India.
Article 324 of the Constitution of India grants powers for the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to the Election Commission.
news.headline: Left Parties and AAP Join CJP Protest Against CEC while Congress Abstains
news.story_lead: The Left parties and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) have decided to participate in a protest organized by Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) against the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). In contrast, the Indian National Congress has chosen to stay away from the agitation. Ahead of the scheduled stir, the Delhi Police enforced traffic and security restrictions, explaining that daily city operations cannot be halted.
news.full_article_text:
### Opposition Alignment and CJP Protest Against CEC

* **Political Participation:** The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Left parties have announced their decision to join a demonstration organized by Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) targeting the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC).
* **Congress Stand:** The Congress party has distanced itself from the CJP-led agitation and decided not to participate.
* **Police Restrictions:** In preparation for the upcoming demonstration, Delhi Police implemented security measures and traffic curbs. Police authorities justified these steps by stating that city mobility and public life cannot be allowed to come to a standstill.
bullet_points: Left parties and AAP are joining the Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) protest against the Chief Election Commissioner.
Congress has decided to stay away from the CJP demonstration.
Delhi Police issued traffic restrictions in response to the planned protest.
Police officials emphasized that capital city movements cannot be brought to a halt.
key_facts: Left parties and AAP are joining the CJP stir against the CEC.
Congress is abstaining from the CJP protest.
Delhi Police imposed movement curbs ahead of the demonstration.
important_dates: 2026-10-10: News report on political parties joining the CJP protest against the CEC
exam_relevance: Relevant for Indian Polity topics relating to constitutional bodies like the Election Commission of India and public order regulation during protests.
news.upsc_analysis: The event highlights political opposition dynamics concerning constitutional institutions and illustrates the urban governance challenge of managing freedom of assembly alongside public order.
causes: Organizing of a demonstration against the Chief Election Commissioner by Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP).
impacts: Deployment of security measures and traffic restrictions in Delhi by police authorities.
challenges: Balancing citizens' right to protest with maintaining traffic movement and public convenience in major urban hubs.
government_steps: Delhi Police enacted security restrictions ahead of the political demonstration to ensure city functions continue.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution governs the Election Commission of India.
way_forward: Ensuring institutional transparency while effectively managing urban traffic and safety during political demonstrations.
news.mains_notes: Protests focused on constitutional authorities highlight debates around institutional governance, political strategy, and city administration maintaining order during mass rallies.
mains_questions: Discuss the constitutional role and autonomy of the Election Commission of India in managing democratic processes.
Examine the challenge faced by police authorities in balancing the right to peaceful protest with public order in urban centers.
news.takeaway: AAP and Left parties join CJP's protest against the CEC, while Congress abstains and Delhi Police enforce restrictions to maintain order.
prelims_facts: Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) organized the demonstration against the Chief Election Commissioner.
Delhi Police issued traffic directives to prevent disruption during the protest.

hindi_translation.story_lead: मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) के खिलाफ 'सिटीज़न फ़ॉर जस्टिस एंड पीस' (CJP) द्वारा आयोजित विरोध प्रदर्शन में वामपंथी दल और आम आदमी पार्टी (AAP) शामिल हो रहे हैं। वहीं, भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने इस प्रदर्शन से दूरी बना ली है। प्रदर्शन को देखते हुए दिल्ली पुलिस ने सुरक्षा और यातायात प्रतिबंध लागू किए हैं।

* **प्रदर्शन में भागीदारी:** आम आदमी पार्टी (AAP) और वामपंथी दलों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) के खिलाफ सिटीज़न फ़ॉर जस्टिस एंड पीस (CJP) के प्रदर्शन में शामिल होने का फैसला किया है।
* **कांग्रेस का रुख:** कांग्रेस पार्टी ने CJP के इस आंदोलन से अलग रहने का फैसला किया है।
* **पुलिस की पाबंदियां:** संभावित प्रदर्शन को देखते हुए दिल्ली पुलिस ने यातायात निर्देश और सुरक्षा प्रबंध लागू किए हैं। पुलिस प्रशासन ने स्पष्ट किया कि शहर के कामकाज और आवाजाही को ठप नहीं होने दिया जा सकता।

कांग्रेस पार्टी ने इस प्रदर्शन में शामिल न होने का फैसला लिया है।
दिल्ली पुलिस ने प्रदर्शन के मद्देनजर यातायात और आवाजाही पर प्रतिबंध लगाए हैं।
पुलिस ने कहा कि राजधानी के कामकाज को पूरी तरह बंद नहीं किया जा सकता।

news.headline: Delhi Encounters Security Restrictions and Transit Disruptions Ahead of CJP Protest
news.story_lead: Ahead of a planned protest organized by the CJP and a call for a Delhi bandh, security authorities implemented strict measures across the heart of the national capital, including the suspension of mobile internet services, road blockades, and restrictions on metro transit. Law enforcement officers on the ground were advised to remain prepared for volatile situations while exercising maximum restraint. The disruptions led to severe impacts on rail transport and a sudden spike in airfares.
news.full_article_text:
Severe preventive security measures were enforced across central Delhi in anticipation of a protest led by the CJP alongside a call for a citywide bandh. Authorities restricted traffic movements, set up blockades on major roads, closed key metro access points, and temporarily suspended mobile internet connectivity in central areas to prevent public disorder.

Frontline police personnel deployed across the city received instructions to prepare for potential unrest while maintaining strict restraint during crowd management duties. The disruptions extended beyond local movement, significantly affecting train operations. In response to the reduced availability of train services, last-minute flight bookings saw a marked increase, driving up airfares significantly.

Political reactions also emerged following the disruptions. Union Minister Chirag Paswan commented on the impact on transport infrastructure, emphasizing that attempts to halt train services would not deter the nation's youth.
bullet_points: Security forces deployed road blockades and restricted metro entry in central Delhi ahead of the CJP protest.
Mobile internet services were temporarily suspended in key areas of the national capital to maintain order.
Police personnel on duty were instructed to prepare for unrest while maintaining restraint.
Train services faced notable disruptions as part of the protest environment.
Demand for last-minute air travel surged, causing airfares to increase sharply.
Union Minister Chirag Paswan publicly reacted to the transit disruptions, advocating for unhindered mobility for youth.
key_facts: Event: Security measures and transit restrictions in Delhi due to a CJP protest and bandh call.
Key measures: Suspension of mobile internet, road blockades, and metro closures in central Delhi.
Directives to police: Stay prepared for intense situations while exercising restraint.
Public impact: Disruption of train services and soaring air travel costs.
important_dates: 2026-10-10: Implementation of citywide security restrictions and transit blockades in Delhi
exam_relevance: Prelims: Understanding administrative powers related to public order maintenance, internet suspension protocols, and reasonable restrictions under Article 19.
Mains: GS Paper II (Governance and Public Order) - Balancing public safety, freedom of assembly, and civic movement during large-scale protests.
news.upsc_analysis: The event highlights the continuous balancing act between administrative measures to maintain public order and the rights of citizens regarding movement and communication. Suspension of internet services and transport blockades are frequently debated in public administration context regarding proportional response and public convenience.
causes: Planned demonstration by the CJP and a call for a Delhi bandh.
impacts: Interruption of mobile internet services and urban transport in central Delhi.
Surge in last-minute airline bookings causing higher airfares for commuters.
challenges: Maintaining law and order without causing excessive disruption to daily civic life.
Ensuring appropriate police restraint during high-tension public demonstrations.
government_steps: Deployment of road blockades and restrictions on public transport access.
Targeted suspension of mobile internet to limit coordination of potential unrest.
Briefing security forces to act with restraint during operations.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution of India concerning freedom of speech and peaceful assembly, subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2) and 19(3).
way_forward: Standardizing urban protest management protocols to minimize transit disruptions and ensure transparent communication with commuters.
news.mains_notes: Key aspects for GS-II: Inter-agency coordination during urban protest management; constitutional provisions on reasonable restrictions; economic impact of transit blockades on citizens.
mains_questions: Discuss the constitutional validity and administrative challenges associated with imposing preventive movement restrictions and digital communication suspensions during public protests in major urban centers.
How can public law enforcement maintain law and order effectively during major public demonstrations while respecting the principle of reasonable restraint?
news.takeaway: Anticipating a CJP protest, Delhi authorities enforced strict transit restrictions and internet suspensions while advising police to maintain restraint amid transport disruptions.
prelims_facts: Mobile internet suspension and urban road/metro blockades were implemented in Delhi in October 2026 ahead of a CJP protest.
Disruptions to rail transport led to a direct increase in last-minute airfares.

hindi_translation.headline: CJP विरोध प्रदर्शन से पहले दिल्ली में सुरक्षा प्रबंध सख्त; मोबाइल इंटरनेट, मेट्रो और मार्ग प्रभावित
hindi_translation.story_lead: CJP के प्रस्तावित विरोध प्रदर्शन और दिल्ली बंद के आह्वान को देखते हुए प्रशासनिक अधिकारियों ने राष्ट्रीय राजधानी के मध्य भाग में मोबाइल इंटरनेट सेवा निलंबित करने, सड़कें बंद करने और मेट्रो संचालन को सीमित करने जैसे कड़े कदम उठाए। ड्यूटी पर तैनात पुलिसकर्मियों को किसी भी स्थिति से निपटने के लिए तैयार रहने तथा संयम बरतने के निर्देश दिए गए।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
CJP द्वारा आयोजित प्रदर्शन और दिल्ली बंद के मद्देनजर राष्ट्रीय राजधानी के प्रमुख क्षेत्रों में व्यापक सुरक्षा उपाय लागू किए गए। कानून-व्यवस्था बनाए रखने के उद्देश्य से प्रशासन ने मध्य दिल्ली में मोबाइल इंटरनेट सेवाएं अस्थायी रूप से बंद कर दीं, मुख्य मार्गों पर बैरिकेडिंग की और मेट्रो स्टेशनों के संचालन में कड़े प्रतिबंध लगाए।

जमीन पर तैनात पुलिसकर्मियों को किसी भी संभावित उपद्रव से निपटने के लिए सतर्क रहने के साथ-साथ भीड़ नियंत्रण के दौरान पूर्ण संयम बरतने के निर्देश दिए गए थे। इन प्रतिबंधों और विरोध प्रदर्शनों के कारण रेल सेवाओं पर भी असर पड़ा, जिससे अंतिम समय में हवाई यात्रा की मांग बढ़ गई और उड़ानों के किराए में भारी बढ़ोतरी दर्ज की गई।

इस स्थिति पर प्रतिक्रिया व्यक्त करते हुए केंद्रीय मंत्री चिराग पासवान ने परिवहन सेवाओं में बाधा उत्पन्न किए जाने पर टिप्पणी की और कहा कि ट्रेनों को रोककर देश के युवाओं को नहीं रोका जा सकता।
bullet_points: CJP प्रदर्शन से पहले मध्य दिल्ली में सड़कें बंद की गईं और मेट्रो सेवाओं पर प्रतिबंध लगाए गए।
सुरक्षा के मद्देनजर कुछ हिस्सों में मोबाइल इंटरनेट सेवाएं अस्थायी रूप से निलंबित की गईं।
पुलिस बल को किसी भी स्थिति से निपटने के लिए तैयार रहने और संयम बरतने की सलाह दी गई।

news.full_article_text: Karnataka SIR gets 1.1 lakh Form 7 objections amid SIR voter list controversy Karnataka has received 110,654 applications seeking objections to proposed entries or deletions of names as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls proceeds Karnataka has received 110,654 applications seeking objections to proposed entries or deletions of names as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls proceeds, with the Election Commission setting October 22 as the deadline to dispose of claims and objections and October 27 for publication of the final roll. The figures, released by the office of Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar on Friday, come amid a political dispute over allegations that bulk Form 7 applications have been used to target voters and police cases against BJP workers who submitted them. BJP state president BY Vijayendra accused the Congress government of using the controversy to intimidate his party’s workers, while defending the revision exercise as an effort to remove irregularities from voter lists. As of October 9, Karnataka had 45,161,393 registered electors: 22,403,422 men, 22,755,113 women and 2,858 transgender voters. Election officials generated 4,382,315 notices during the revision, delivering 4,373,745, or 99.80% of them. Hearings had been completed for 4,088,099 of the delivered notices, representing 93.47%, while 285,646 cases remained pending. The final hearing is scheduled for October 12. Between June 16 and October 8, the state received 23,02,215 applications under four categories. These comprised 9,52,497 Form 6 applications for inclusion in electoral rolls, 4,712 Form 6A applications from Indian citizens living abroad seeking enrolment, 1,10,654 Form 7 applications seeking objections to proposed inclusions or deletion of existing entries, and 12,34,352 Form 8 applications for corrections, changes of address and replacement of voter identity cards. The Chief Electoral Officer’s office said constituency-wise information on claims and objections submitted through Forms 9, 10, 11, 11A and 11B had been published on the Election Commission of India’s website. In a letter dated October 1, Anbukkumar drew the attention of Electoral Registration Officers to complaints about bulk Form 7 submissions and questions about their authenticity. The communication directed District Election Officers, Additional District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers to initiate proceedings under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against applicants found to have knowingly made false written statements or declarations in Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8. An inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, must precede such action, the letter said. Vijayendra said the BJP was supporting the SIR process rather than defending the Election Commission against allegations surrounding its conduct. “The BJP is not trying to defend the Election Commission of India. Our position is that Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a process intended to cleanse electoral rolls and remove irregularities,” he told a press conference on Friday. He questioned why the BJP should answer for the conduct of an exercise administered by the Election Commission and accused the Congress government of pressuring the police to register cases against party workers over Form 7 applications. Vijayendra argued that Booth Level Officers involved in the revision worked under the state government, and said applications from political parties should be assessed on their merits. “If a Form-7 application is submitted by the BJP or by any other political party, the Returning Officer will accept it if it is valid and reject if it is incorrect,” he said. The BJP leader accused Chief Minister DK Shivakumar of using the dispute to target his party and alleged that the Congress was portraying the applications as an attempt to remove votes belonging to AHINDA communities, a term used for minorities, backward classes and Dalits. “We have no need to resort to such conspiracies. We have submitted applications wherever there are doubts about entries in the electoral rolls. If the applications are valid, they will be accepted; if they are incorrect, they will be rejected,” Vijayendra said. He denied that the BJP had singled out any community, saying its objections concerned deceased voters and duplicate entries. He also alleged that illegal Bangladeshi immigrants were being included in electoral rolls in Bengaluru and other Assembly constituencies in Karnataka. Vijayendra referred to interim relief reportedly granted by the Karnataka High Court’s Dharwad Bench in a case related to the dispute and accused the Congress government of trying to intimidate BJP workers through police cases. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arun Dev Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

Karnataka has received 110,654 applications seeking objections to proposed entries or deletions of names as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls proceeds, with the Election Commission setting October 22 as the deadline to dispose of claims and objections and October 27 for publication of the final roll.

The figures, released by the office of Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar on Friday, come amid a political dispute over allegations that bulk Form 7 applications have been used to target voters and police cases against BJP workers who submitted them. BJP state president BY Vijayendra accused the Congress government of using the controversy to intimidate his party’s workers, while defending the revision exercise as an effort to remove irregularities from voter lists.
As of October 9, Karnataka had 45,161,393 registered electors: 22,403,422 men, 22,755,113 women and 2,858 transgender voters.

Election officials generated 4,382,315 notices during the revision, delivering 4,373,745, or 99.80% of them. Hearings had been completed for 4,088,099 of the delivered notices, representing 93.47%, while 285,646 cases remained pending. The final hearing is scheduled for October 12.

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Karnataka SIR gets 1.1 lakh Form 7 objections amid SIR voter list controversy Karnataka has received 110,654 applications seeking objections to proposed entries or deletions of names as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls proceeds Karnataka has received 110,654 applications seeking objections to proposed entries or deletions of names as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls proceeds, with the Election Commission setting October 22 as the deadline to dispose of claims and objections and October 27 for publication of the final roll. The figures, released by the office of Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar on Friday, come amid a political dispute over allegations that bulk Form 7 applications have been used to target voters and police cases against BJP workers who submitted them. BJP state president BY Vijayendra accused the Congress government of using the controversy to intimidate his party’s workers, while defending the revision exercise as an effort to remove irregularities from voter lists. As of October 9, Karnataka had 45,161,393 registered electors: 22,403,422 men, 22,755,113 women and 2,858 transgender voters. Election officials generated 4,382,315 notices during the revision, delivering 4,373,745, or 99.80% of them. Hearings had been completed for 4,088,099 of the delivered notices, representing 93.47%, while 285,646 cases remained pending. The final hearing is scheduled for October 12. Between June 16 and October 8, the state received 23,02,215 applications under four categories. These comprised 9,52,497 Form 6 applications for inclusion in electoral rolls, 4,712 Form 6A applications from Indian citizens living abroad seeking enrolment, 1,10,654 Form 7 applications seeking objections to proposed inclusions or deletion of existing entries, and 12,34,352 Form 8 applications for corrections, changes of address and replacement of voter identity cards. The Chief Electoral Officer’s office said constituency-wise information on claims and objections submitted through Forms 9, 10, 11, 11A and 11B had been published on the Election Commission of India’s website. In a letter dated October 1, Anbukkumar drew the attention of Electoral Registration Officers to complaints about bulk Form 7 submissions and questions about their authenticity. The communication directed District Election Officers, Additional District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers to initiate proceedings under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against applicants found to have knowingly made false written statements or declarations in Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8. An inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, must precede such action, the letter said. Vijayendra said the BJP was supporting the SIR process rather than defending the Election Commission against allegations surrounding its conduct. “The BJP is not trying to defend the Election Commission of India. Our position is that Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a process intended to cleanse electoral rolls and remove irregularities,” he told a press conference on Friday. He questioned why the BJP should answer for the conduct of an exercise administered by the Election Commission and accused the Congress government of pressuring the police to register cases against party workers over Form 7 applications. Vijayendra argued that Booth Level Officers involved in the revision worked under the state government, and said applications from political parties should be assessed on their merits. “If a Form-7 application is submitted by the BJP or by any other political party, the Returning Officer will accept it if it is valid and reject if it is incorrect,” he said. The BJP leader accused Chief Minister DK Shivakumar of using the dispute to target his party and alleged that the Congress was portraying the applications as an attempt to remove votes belonging to AHINDA communities, a term used for minorities, backward classes and Dalits. “We have no need to resort to such conspiracies. We have submitted applications wherever there are doubts about entries in the electoral rolls. If the applications are valid, they will be accepted; if they are incorrect, they will be rejected,” Vijayendra said. He denied that the BJP had singled out any community, saying its objections concerned deceased voters and duplicate entries. He also alleged that illegal Bangladeshi immigrants were being included in electoral rolls in Bengaluru and other Assembly constituencies in Karnataka. Vijayendra referred to interim relief reportedly granted by the Karnataka High Court’s Dharwad Bench in a case related to the dispute and accused the Congress government of trying to intimidate BJP workers through police cases. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arun Dev Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

news.headline: Ajmer businessman robbed of ₹3 crore jewellery by group posed as fake IT officials, six held: Police
news.story_lead: Ajmer businessman robbed of ₹3 crore jewellery by group posed as fake IT officials, six held: Police Six people were arrested within three hours of a ₹ 3 crore jewellery robbery in Ajmer, where a group allegedly posing as Income Tax officials targeted a businessman’s home. Six people were arrested within three hours of a daylight robbery in which a group allegedly posing as Income Tax (IT) Department officials stole gold and silver jewellery worth an estimated ₹ 3 crore from a 29-year-old businessman’s house in Rajasthan’s Ajmer district, police said on Friday. According to the police, around nine to ten people arrived at Anil Maheshwari’s house in Mahesh Vihar Colony near the Dilwara bypass around 11.30 am, displayed fake identity cards and claimed to be conducting an official search.
news.full_article_text: Ajmer businessman robbed of ₹3 crore jewellery by group posed as fake IT officials, six held: Police Six people were arrested within three hours of a ₹ 3 crore jewellery robbery in Ajmer, where a group allegedly posing as Income Tax officials targeted a businessman’s home. Six people were arrested within three hours of a daylight robbery in which a group allegedly posing as Income Tax (IT) Department officials stole gold and silver jewellery worth an estimated ₹ 3 crore from a 29-year-old businessman’s house in Rajasthan’s Ajmer district, police said on Friday. According to the police, around nine to ten people arrived at Anil Maheshwari’s house in Mahesh Vihar Colony near the Dilwara bypass around 11.30 am, displayed fake identity cards and claimed to be conducting an official search. The accused allegedly searched the house, collected jewellery from a cupboard and threatened the family members against raising an alarm before fleeing with the valuables. A case was registered at Nasirabad Sadar police station. Ajmer superintendent of police (SP) Harshvardhan Agrawala said multiple teams were formed to identify and apprehend the suspects. Police examined CCTV footage from the crime scene and adjoining areas, analysed technical evidence and tracked the suspects’ movements before arresting six of them within three hours of the incident. Police identified the six arrested people as Devendra (33), from Madarpura in Ajmer; Sanjay Rawat (34), from Sendariya; Ravikant alias Ravi (40), from Dholabhata; Amit (26), from Parbatpura; Tara (39), from Rohisa in Nagaur district; and Deva alias Devendra Singh Rawat (20), from Madarpura. Preliminary investigation suggests that the robbery was planned over a month, police officers said. One of the suspects, Devendra, had worked at the complainant’s house between 2016 and 2021, while another suspect, Sanjay Rawat, reportedly knew the businessman professionally. Police suspect that the accused used their familiarity with the complainant and his financial circumstances to plan the robbery. Sanjay allegedly coordinated with the other accused, while the group arranged fake identity cards and posed as income tax officials to gain entry to the house without raising suspicion. Police said the investigation was continuing to recover the stolen jewellery, establish the roles of other suspects and determine whether the accused were involved in similar crimes.

news.full_article_text: Sonam Wangchuk backs CJP stir in Delhi, but says he can't attend: 'Hope we won't let Bapu down' Sonam Wangchuk won't attend CJP's October 10 protest in Delhi, cites winter preps Activist Sonam Wangchuk said on Friday that he won't be participating in the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP )'s Jantar Mantar protest on October 10, saying that he is busy making preparations for the upcoming winter. The Ladakh-based activist quoted Urdu poet Faiz Ahmed Faiz as he listed the winter preparations that included ‘making artificial glaciers for water security and experiments for GLOF or glacial lake flood security and to diffuse the 200+ ticking water bombs in high Himalayas.’ Track latest updates on anti-CEC protest in Delhi The CJP is holding a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 as part of its nationwide campaign demanding CEC Gyanesh Kuamr's resignation over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) irregularities. “Despite all efforts of the government to hinder & damage our work we continue to work for national security... making preparations as another winter comes,” Wangchuk wrote on X, as he extended his wishes to the protesters and urged them to remain ‘peaceful at all costs’. Quoting Faiz, he wrote, “Aur Bhi Gham Hain Zamaane Main Siyaast Ke Siva…Rahaten aur bhi hain wasl ki raahat ke siva.” “I hope we won't let Baapu down,” he wrote. Wangchuk was one of the key figures of CJP's July protest when the youth-led movement took to streets demanding the then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over examination irregularities. The activist sat on a a hunger strike for 26 days at Jantar Mantar in support of the protesting students and ended the indefinite strike on July 23 at a hospital in Gurugram in the presence of union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying that he broke the fast after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. CJP's October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar The CJP's October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar has prompted unprecedented security clampdown across the national capital as Delhi Police denied permission for the stir. Extensive security arranagements have been announced including inetrnet shutdown around Jantar Mantar, closure of 45 metri stations, deployment of additional 25,000 police and intensive checks at city's border points, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels and other sensitive locations. Internet services will be suspended within a 4-kilometre radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on October 9 to 10 pm on October 10. The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones to strengthen security arrangements and maintain law and order. Each of the 20 zones will be monitored by a Joint Commissioner of Police, a Deputy Commissioner of Police and an Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police to ensure close supervision of the security arrangements, the sources said. Train services have also been disrupted as nearly two dozen North Central Railway (NCR), Northern Railway (NR), and North Eastern Railway (NER) trains originating from various Uttar Pradesh cities and connecting the state to Delhi have been cancelled ahead of the CJP protest. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. news.headline: Election Commission caps Form 7 applications to 10 per elector during claims-and-objections period
news.story_lead: Election Commission caps Form 7 applications to 10 per elector during claims-and-objections period The Election Commission has capped Form 7 applications at 10 per elector during the claims period and five a month during continuous electoral roll updation. The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday set a ceiling on the number of Form 7 applications a single elector can file, saying bulk objections on “unsubstantiated grounds” were inconveniencing voters and overloading field staff. In an instruction to the chief electoral officers of all states and Union territories (UTs), the poll body said an individual elector can file at most 10 Form 7 applications during the entire claims-and-objections period.
news.full_article_text: Election Commission caps Form 7 applications to 10 per elector during claims-and-objections period The Election Commission has capped Form 7 applications at 10 per elector during the claims period and five a month during continuous electoral roll updation. The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday set a ceiling on the number of Form 7 applications a single elector can file, saying bulk objections on “unsubstantiated grounds” were inconveniencing voters and overloading field staff. In an instruction to the chief electoral officers of all states and Union territories (UTs), the poll body said an individual elector can file at most 10 Form 7 applications during the entire claims-and-objections period. During continuous updation of electoral rolls, the cap is five per month. The limits apply to both online and offline filings, it said. The Commission said that while online filings were capped at six at a time, “the number of physical forms presented in bulk has not been defined and has been left to the judgement of the Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), which is creating challenges for the field functionaries.” Form 7 is used to object to the inclusion of a name in the electoral roll or to seek deletion, and can be filed only by a person already registered in that constituency. The Manual on Electoral Rolls already says bulk claims by an individual should not be entertained. More recently, Form 7 has been at the centre of a controversy after cases of its alleged misuse were reported from Karnataka, Telangana and Rajasthan. In Telangana, the Congress first raised the issue in Hyderabad’s Musheerabad on October 1, alleging that a BJP booth-level agent had filed more than 30 Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of members of a single Muslim family. Similar bulk applications were reported in the Bahadurpura and Goshamahal constituencies, with pre-filled forms that left the applicant details blank. The poll body also told EROs to reject forms with incomplete details or without the objector’s original signature, noting that a seal cannot replace it. They must verify the applicant against the electoral roll, issue a notice and hear the objector separately for each form, and give the person whose name is being challenged an opportunity to be heard before passing an order. Where a complaint is found to be false or fabricated, the ERO shall act under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which penalises false declarations. For the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), booth-level agents of recognised parties remain bound by existing caps of 50 forms a day before draft publication and 10 a day after. - Election Commission Of India

news.story_lead: 'Shocked that President accepted what we said': Rahul Gandhi makes big claim after meet over CEC row A delegation of Opposition MPs met President Murmu on Friday and submitted the memorandum over SIR irregulariries. After meeting President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that he was "shocked" that she accepted the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chore' rather than denying it. The Opposition MPs met the President amid the ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
news.full_article_text: 'Shocked that President accepted what we said': Rahul Gandhi makes big claim after meet over CEC row A delegation of Opposition MPs met President Murmu on Friday and submitted the memorandum over SIR irregulariries. After meeting President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that he was "shocked" that she accepted the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chore' rather than denying it. The Opposition MPs met the President amid the ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Following the meeting, Gandhi said that the President accepted the statement and sought proof of ‘vote chori’. The 10-member delegation included Rahul Gandhi, accompanied by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. Also read: DMRC revises order after Supreme Court rap, 45 Delhi Metro stations to remain affected The bloc's regional heavyweights were represented by Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Samajwadi Party leader Rajiv Rai, NCP leader Supriya Sule and National Conference leader Omar Abdullah. Deep Dive “Our memorandum to the President clearly said that PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar have conspired to destroy Indian democracy” Gandhi was quoted as saying. Rahul Gandhi quotes Nehru ahead of meeting with President Before meeting President Murmu, Gandhi recalled India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's iconic 1947 address at the Parliament's Central Hall where the INDIA bloc MPs had gathered before march to Rashtrapati Bhavan. The address recalled the foundational promises of Indian democracy as the INDIA bloc stepped up its joint offensive against the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging institutional bias and political partiality. A new star rises, the star of freedom in the East, a new hope comes into being, a vision long cherished materialises. May the star never set and that hope never be betrayed..." Rahul Gandhi was quoted as saying by news agency ANI. Meanwhile, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge slammed the government for imposing curbs in Delhi as 57 metro stations will remain shut in view of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10. Kharge accused the government of acting out of fear. "They are afraid. The Opposition MPs met the President amid the ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
hindi_translation.full_article_text: 'Shocked that President accepted what we said': Rahul Gandhi makes big claim after meet over CEC row A delegation of Opposition MPs met President Murmu on Friday and submitted the memorandum over SIR irregulariries. After meeting President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that he was "shocked" that she accepted the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chore' rather than denying it. The Opposition MPs met the President amid the ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Following the meeting, Gandhi said that the President accepted the statement and sought proof of ‘vote chori’. Track latest updates on anti-CEC row “I just sat in quite an unbelievable meeting with the President of India. We presented our memorandum to her outlining PM Modi and HM Amit Shah’s gross subversion of India’s electoral system and seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. I was shocked that the President did not deny Vote Chori,” Gandhi wrote on X. Also read: Inside Opposition’s 4-point memorandum to President Murmu: What Rahul Gandhi, Kharge demanded Gandhi said that he told the President that proof of 'election chori' is known to country as state after state has been stolen. A 10-member Opposition delegation addressed the press on the outcome of their representation to the President. The 10-member delegation included Rahul Gandhi, accompanied by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. Also read: DMRC revises order after Supreme Court rap, 45 Delhi Metro stations to remain affected The bloc's regional heavyweights were represented by Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Samajwadi Party leader Rajiv Rai, NCP leader Supriya Sule and National Conference leader Omar Abdullah. Deep Dive “Our memorandum to the President clearly said that PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar have conspired to destroy Indian democracy” Gandhi was quoted as saying. Rahul Gandhi quotes Nehru ahead of meeting with President Before meeting President Murmu, Gandhi recalled India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru's iconic 1947 address at the Parliament's Central Hall where the INDIA bloc MPs had gathered before march to Rashtrapati Bhavan. The address recalled the foundational promises of Indian democracy as the INDIA bloc stepped up its joint offensive against the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging institutional bias and political partiality. Also read: Sonam Wangchuk backs CJP stir in Delhi, but says he can't attend: 'Hope we won't let Bapu down' "Jawaharlal Nehru gave a very famous speech. It was given from the Central Hall of Parliament on 14 August 1947. I want to quote a little bit from it. It is a fateful moment for us in India, for all Asia and for the world. A new star rises, the star of freedom in the East, a new hope comes into being, a vision long cherished materialises. May the star never set and that hope never be betrayed..." Rahul Gandhi was quoted as saying by news agency ANI. Meanwhile, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge slammed the government for imposing curbs in Delhi as 57 metro stations will remain shut in view of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10. Kharge accused the government of acting out of fear. "They are afraid. A person who is afraid will die tomorrow, if not today."Kharge said. “The mistakes committed by Gyanesh Kumar have created a situation of fear in the country and put democracy in danger. That is why we are going to meet the President and apprise her of the things he has done". - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. In the meantime, she thought it was a good idea to share what she learnt, hence took up part-time teaching of journalism course at Jamia Millia Islamia, which she says, she thoroughly enjoyed-not sure if the feeling was mutual. For a year, she also tried her hands at communication roles, only to realise she was more comfortable with news. So, joined HT in September 2025. Not much of a talker, always up for chai and sarcasm. And pun always intended. Her tag line is 'I will figure out, but I need to panic first' Read More

news.headline: 'Final call': Dipke releases video message ahead of CJP protest, anticipates arrest upon landing in Delhi
news.story_lead: 'Final call': Dipke releases video message ahead of CJP protest, anticipates arrest upon landing in Delhi Dipke said he would travel from Mumbai to Delhi on morning of October and urged people to join the protest in large numbers CJP's Abhijeet Dipke , in a final video appeal ahead of the protest at Jantar Mantar over CEC row in Delhi on October 10, said he was unsure whether he would be arrested upon landing in the national capital but asserted that he would not back down from the fight for free and fair elections. The CJP is leading a massive demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Dipke said he would travel from Mumbai to Delhi on Saturday morning and urged people to join the protest in large numbers.

bullet_points: 'Final call': Dipke releases video message ahead of CJP protest, anticipates arrest upon landing in Delhi
Dipke said he would travel from Mumbai to Delhi on morning of October and urged people to join the protest in large numbers

CJP's Abhijeet Dipke , in a final video appeal ahead of the protest at Jantar Mantar over CEC row in Delhi on October 10, said he was unsure whether he would be arrested upon landing in the national capital but asserted that he would not back down from the fight for free and fair elections.

The CJP is leading a massive demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Dipke said he would travel from Mumbai to Delhi on Saturday morning and urged people to join the protest in large numbers. He added that he was not afraid of being detained or arrested, or of facing charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or the National Security Act (NSA).

"I am not scared (even) if I am detained or arrested. The government can slap NSA or UAPA against me. CJP wants free and fair polls and that cannot happen without (Chief Election Commissioner) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation or scrapping of SIR or neutral procedure to appoint election commissioner," he said, asking people to come to Jantar Mantar in large numbers.
“This is a fight to save our country's democracy,” Dipke said, reiterating the CJP's demand for free and fair elections.
