news.exam_corner_topic: ECI fortified, 254 trains cancelled, metro affected, internet shut: Delhi braces for CJP's October 10 protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
news.headline: ECI fortified, 254 trains cancelled, metro affected, internet shut: Delhi braces for CJP's October 10 protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
news.story_lead: ECI fortified, 254 trains cancelled, metro affected, internet shut: Delhi braces for CJP's October 10 protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Delhi Police has imposed Section 163 BNSS restrictions in ‘sensitive areas’ to maintain public order and prevent potential security threats. Delhi has tightened security ahead of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10, with restrictions on mobile internet, metro access, train services and commercial establishments expected to affect daily life across parts of the national capital. The protest, organised by the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) and student groups, seeks the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
news.full_article_text: ECI fortified, 254 trains cancelled, metro affected, internet shut: Delhi braces for CJP's October 10 protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Delhi Police has imposed Section 163 BNSS restrictions in ‘sensitive areas’ to maintain public order and prevent potential security threats. Delhi has tightened security ahead of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10, with restrictions on mobile internet, metro access, train services and commercial establishments expected to affect daily life across parts of the national capital. The protest, organised by the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) and student groups, seeks the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The INDIA bloc has also separately been protesting against the Election Commission, accusing it of failing to ensure free and fair elections. No permission to protest: Delhi Police Authorities have imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), deployed additional security personnel and restricted access to several sensitive locations. Deep Dive Delhi Police has denied permission for Saturday’s demonstration, citing the late submission of the application and alleged violations during an earlier protest. ALSO READ | No permission for Jantar Mantar protest, Delhi Police say CJP's intimation came 'too late' ECI office fortified Access to Ashoka Road towards the Election Commission of India (ECI) headquarters has been blocked with a bus near the Sansad Marg–Ashoka Road roundabout. Barricades have been placed outside the ECI headquarters, with security personnel deployed in large numbers. Mobile internet to remain suspended for 24 hours The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has approved a 24-hour suspension of mobile internet services in a four-kilometre radius around the Janpath-Kartavya Path area in New Delhi. The shutdown began at 10 pm on Friday and will continue until 10 pm on Saturday. Authorities have issued the order on public security grounds under the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024. The order specifically concerns mobile internet services within the notified zone. ALSO READ | 'Don't use hammer to kill a fly': Supreme Court asks Centre, Delhi Police to lift blanket curbs on metro, trains 45 metro stations closed The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) revised its earlier decision to close 57 metro stations after the Supreme Court intervened on Friday. The court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to lift blanket restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of the proposed demonstration. It said security arrangements should not completely shut down public transport or cause widespread inconvenience to ordinary commuters. Under the revised advisory, entry and exit gates at 45 listed metro stations will remain closed from 9 pm on October 9 until 6 pm on October 10. Security agencies will review the situation before deciding on further restrictions. The affected stations include Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Lok Kalyan Marg, Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Seva Teerth, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, among others. Check full list of the 45 affected Delhi Metro stations here . Interchange facilities will remain available at the affected stations, except at New Delhi station. Passengers will not be able to enter or exit through the affected stations during the notified period. Delhi Traffic Police warns of diversions The Delhi Traffic Police has warned of traffic disruptions across the capital on Saturday, ahead of the CJP protest. Diversions may begin at 6 am, depending on the situation, affecting areas such as Dhaula Kuan, Mandi House, Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar Road, Patel Chowk and Sansad Marg. Commuters heading to railway stations, bus terminals and the airport have been advised to allow extra travel time and avoid unnecessary journeys. Traffic restrictions may change depending on the situation. ALSO READ | Delhi Police issue traffic advisory ahead of CJP protest tomorrow: Diversions likely from 6 am; check affected routes 254 trains cancelled on Saturday A total of 254 trains, including 75 Mail and Express trains and 179 local trains, have been cancelled between 4 am and 2 pm on Saturday. The cancellations will affect short-distance routes connecting Delhi with Ghaziabad, Meerut, Panipat and Kurukshetra, among other destinations. Services such as the Howrah–New Delhi Rajdhani Express, Tejas Rajdhani Express, Magadh Express, Sampoorna Kranti Express and Shaan-e-Bhopal Express are among the affected trains, HT reported earlier. The security plan also includes checks at Delhi's entry points and restrictions in sensitive areas. Connaught Place shops advised to shut The New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA) has advised shops, offices, restaurants and other commercial establishments in Connaught Place to remain closed on Saturday as a precautionary measure. In a circular issued on Friday, NDTA president Atul Bhargava asked business owners and occupants to remain vigilant and cooperate with the advisory to reduce the risk of property damage and injuries during the expected demonstrations. Jantar Mantar, a key protest location in the capital, is preparing for the CJP-led mobilisation. Connaught Place and nearby areas could also experience heightened security checks and restrictions on movement. Liquor shops closed on October 10 Retail liquor shops across Delhi will remain closed on Saturday under a two-day dry-day order issued by the Delhi Excise Department amid the security arrangements. ALSO READ | All liquor shops in Delhi to remain shut for 2 days in view of CJP protest: ‘Preventive measure for public order’ Section 163 restrictions in force Delhi Police has imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS in “sensitive areas”. The provisions allow authorities to issue urgent orders to prevent potential threats to public safety and maintain public order. Police have erected barricades and restricted access to roads around Jantar Mantar and Parliament Street. The restrictions are intended to prevent unauthorised gatherings and manage the movement of crowds around high-security locations. Police register 27 FIRs over seven days of protests Law enforcement agencies have registered 27 First Information Reports (FIRs) over a seven-day period of protests targeting CEC Gyanesh Kumar, according news agency ANI. Police have relied on provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) dealing with collective criminal responsibility, disobedience of public orders, obstruction of public servants and the use of force against officials. Section 3(5) of the BNS, which deals with joint criminal liability when multiple people act with a common intention, was invoked in 22 of the 27 FIRs. news.headline: ‘Gaurav Gogoi failed completely, should resign’: Akhil Gogoi slams Congress after Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll setback
news.story_lead: ‘Gaurav Gogoi failed completely, should resign’: Akhil Gogoi slams Congress after Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll setback Akhil Gogoi also blamed Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi for the party's poor performance and called for his immediate resignation. The BJP won the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election in Assam, with the Congress being pushed to the third place. The result has drawn sharp criticism from Raijor Dal chief Akhil Gogoi, a former ally of the Congress, who called the defeat a “tragedy for Assam's anti-BJP forces”.
news.full_article_text: ‘Gaurav Gogoi failed completely, should resign’: Akhil Gogoi slams Congress after Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll setback Akhil Gogoi also blamed Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi for the party's poor performance and called for his immediate resignation. The BJP won the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election in Assam, with the Congress being pushed to the third place. The result has drawn sharp criticism from Raijor Dal chief Akhil Gogoi, a former ally of the Congress, who called the defeat a “tragedy for Assam's anti-BJP forces”. Akhil Gogoi also blamed Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi for the party's poor performance and called for his immediate resignation. His remarks come as the Congress struggles in a constituency where Muslims account for more than 55% of voters. Akhil Gogoi questions Congress's performance in Nagaon Reacting to the by-election results, Raijor Dal MLA Akhil Gogoi pointed to the sharp fall in the Congress's vote count. He noted that the constituency had previously been held by the Congress, but a candidate's move to the BJP led to the by-election. “Regarding the by-election in Nagaon—it was originally a Congress seat, but the candidate switched to the BJP, which is why this by-election is taking place,” he was quoted as saying by news agency ANI. Akhil Gogoi said the Congress had won the seat by a margin of 2.5 lakh votes in the previous election but was now struggling to reach even two lakh votes. “This is essentially a minority-dominated seat,” he said, adding that the Congress's minority vote share had fallen sharply. “The most significant development this time is that the minority vote share for Congress has plummeted from 25% to just 5%. The BJP is poised to win this minority-dominated seat,” he said. Calling the outcome a historic setback for the Congress, Akhil Gogoi said Gaurav Gogoi had failed in his role as state party president. “This is a historic defeat for the Congress,” he said. “I believe the Congress President, Gaurav Gogoi, has failed completely. In my opinion, Gaurav Gogoi should resign from the post of State Congress President this very day.” Amit Shah credits BJP leadership for bypoll victories Union Home Minister Amit Shah welcomed the BJP-led NDA's performance in the by-elections in West Bengal, Assam and Puducherry, as well as recent local body polls in Rajasthan and Tripura. In a post shared on X, Shah said the results reflected continued public support for the BJP under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership. “The BJP, under the leadership of PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji, continues to win elections one after another despite the lies and disinformation campaigns run by Rahul Gandhi and the INDI Alliance,” Shah said. He claimed that the results showed voters had rejected the opposition alliance. “The NDA’s victories in the by-elections in West Bengal, Assam and Puducherry, and the recently held local body polls in Rajasthan and Tripura, demonstrate that the people have completely rejected the INDI Alliance,” he said. news.headline: Trump says Iran war will be ‘over soon’, claims US stopped Tehran from getting nuclear weapon
news.story_lead: Trump says Iran war will be ‘over soon’, claims US stopped Tehran from getting nuclear weapon Speaking at a White House event, Trump also predicted that gas prices would fall, saying the conflict would end “one way or the other”. US President Donald Trump on Friday said the war with Iran will be “over soon”, claiming that the United States had stopped Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. Speaking at a White House event, Trump also predicted that gas prices would fall, saying the conflict would end “one way or the other”.
news.full_article_text: Trump says Iran war will be ‘over soon’, claims US stopped Tehran from getting nuclear weapon Speaking at a White House event, Trump also predicted that gas prices would fall, saying the conflict would end “one way or the other”. US President Donald Trump on Friday said the war with Iran will be “over soon”, claiming that the United States had stopped Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. Speaking at a White House event, Trump also predicted that gas prices would fall, saying the conflict would end “one way or the other”. “We stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon — and the prices will come tumbling and it’s gonna be over soon, one way or the other,” Trump said. He also said he remained open to direct negotiations with Tehran but rejected its proposal, citing uncertainty over who was leading the country. “Always open to direct talks; the biggest problem is that nobody knows who is running the country. I reject their proposal,” Trump said. Trump rules out Iran strikes before November 3 elections Trump said on Thursday that he would not order the US military to resume strikes against Iran before the November 3 midterm elections. In a social media post, he said the US “will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.” The president also said his administration had been “having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran.” Trump has recently suggested that the war could reach a turning point shortly before or after the midterm elections. At the same time, he has kept open the possibility of restarting full-scale military operations against Iran. news.exam_corner_topic: SC directs Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to provide full treatment to Delhi acid attack survivor
news.headline: SC directs Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to provide full treatment to Delhi acid attack survivor
news.story_lead: SC directs Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to provide full treatment to Delhi acid attack survivor The Supreme Court has directed Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in Delhi to provide an acid attack survivor full treatment, including plastic surgery and medicines, regardless of cost. The Supreme Court on Friday directed Delhi’s Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to ensure that full treatment is provided to an acid attack survivor until she is fit to be discharged, after it was told that the hospital had asked the victim to get admitted to Safdarjung Hospital for further treatment. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant took up the matter on an urgent mention by Shaheen Malik, an acid attack survivor whose organisation, Brave Souls Foundation, works for the rehabilitation and welfare of acid attack victims.
news.full_article_text: SC directs Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to provide full treatment to Delhi acid attack survivor The Supreme Court has directed Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in Delhi to provide an acid attack survivor full treatment, including plastic surgery and medicines, regardless of cost. The Supreme Court on Friday directed Delhi’s Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to ensure that full treatment is provided to an acid attack survivor until she is fit to be discharged, after it was told that the hospital had asked the victim to get admitted to Safdarjung Hospital for further treatment. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant took up the matter on an urgent mention by Shaheen Malik, an acid attack survivor whose organisation, Brave Souls Foundation, works for the rehabilitation and welfare of acid attack victims. Malik pointed out that the victim suffered the acid attack in Delhi’s Bhajanpura area on October 6 and, despite being entitled under the law to free medical treatment, was being denied the same by leading private hospitals in Delhi. While the victim is still at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital (SGRH), Malik said the hospital told her on Friday to leave as it does not have a dedicated burn ward. Malik also contacted Apollo Hospital but received a similar response. The bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said, “The application raises alarming facts.” Malik said, “Both the eyes of the victim are damaged. The Ganga Ram hospital wants to refer her to a government hospital. Why should the victim go to a government hospital when the law entitles her free treatment at any hospital.” Her application cited Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), which stipulates that all hospitals, whether public or private, run by the Central government, state government, local bodies or any other person, shall immediately provide first-aid medical treatment, free of cost, to acid attack victims. The bench directed, “We direct the management of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital to keep the acid attack victim as an indoor patient and provide her all facilities, including medicines, plastic surgery and any other treatment, irrespective of the cost of such treatment.” The court directed the hospital to forward the bill to the court and further held, “The victim shall not be discharged till she is in a position to be discharged and would require only outdoor treatment.” The application by Malik pointed out that soon after the incident, the victim was taken to the Delhi government-run GTB Hospital, from where she sought discharge on October 8 to SGRH. She arrived at the hospital the same day at around 4 pm but was admitted to the emergency department after a long wait of nearly three hours. “Apart from administering first-aid dressings, no substantive medical treatment was provided to the victim, thereby leaving her without the requisite medical care despite the urgent and serious nature of her acid attack injuries,” the application said. On Friday, the victim’s family was asked to prepare for discharge and approach another hospital capable of providing the requisite treatment. Following this, Malik filed an application and appealed to the CJI for an urgent hearing. The court directed the Registry to list the application along with a pending matter filed by Malik relating to acid attack victims. - Sir Ganga Ram Hospital - Acid Attack Survivor

news.headline: Public safety, past lapses: Why Delhi Police denied CJP permission for Jantar Mantar protest
news.story_lead: Public safety, past lapses: Why Delhi Police denied CJP permission for Jantar Mantar protest Delhi police said the right to protest is a fundamental right but that granting permission also requires authorities to consider the rights of other citizens. Delhi Police has denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, citing short notice, alleged violations during earlier demonstrations and concerns over public safety and law and order. The police also defended the restrictions imposed in New Delhi, saying they were necessary to prevent overcrowding and ensure the safety of protesters, residents and commuters.
news.full_article_text: Public safety, past lapses: Why Delhi Police denied CJP permission for Jantar Mantar protest Delhi police said the right to protest is a fundamental right but that granting permission also requires authorities to consider the rights of other citizens. Delhi Police has denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, citing short notice, alleged violations during earlier demonstrations and concerns over public safety and law and order. The police also defended the restrictions imposed in New Delhi, saying they were necessary to prevent overcrowding and ensure the safety of protesters, residents and commuters. In a letter dated October 9, addressed to CJP co-convener Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna, the New Delhi district police said the group's communication submitted on October 7 was merely an intimation of the proposed protest and did not constitute a duly submitted application seeking permission. The police said existing guidelines require applications for programmes at Jantar Mantar to be submitted at least 10 days before the intended date. Deep Dive The police said the right to protest is a fundamental right but that granting permission also requires authorities to consider the rights of other citizens and residents. It cited traffic congestion, safety concerns and the potential disruption of public life as reasons for regulating demonstrations. Why Delhi Police is citing earlier protests The police referred to the July protests at Jantar Mantar, saying permission had been granted for a one-day demonstration but that it continued for around a month. In its statement on X, the police said more than 200 personnel were injured during the protests and alleged that the participation of people with criminal antecedents contributed to the violence. Hindustan Times reported on July 27, citing Delhi Police officials, that police had identified 2,873 people through CCTV footage linked to the July 20 march towards Parliament. Of these, 989 were found to have criminal antecedents, according to the officials. The cases included murder, robbery, sexual assault and other offences. The police claims about the criminal antecedents of those identified were attributed to officials and should not be read as convictions. The July 20 march saw clashes at several locations in central Delhi. An FIR accessed by HT alleged that protesters assaulted police personnel, damaged public property and attempted to breach Parliament security. The allegations formed part of the police account of the violence. In its October 9 letter, Delhi Police said the continuation of an earlier CJP protest beyond the permitted hours had resulted in serious law and order problems and a deterioration in public order. The police also claimed that women constables had been molested and assaulted by people protesting at Jantar Mantar during the previous week, describing the incidents as deeply troubling. CJP had estimated 500-600 people for June protest Documents submitted by CJP to Delhi Police show that the group had estimated a gathering of 500-600 people for its June 20 demonstration at Jantar Mantar. In an application dated June 17, the group said the protest would be against alleged irregularities and paper leaks in competitive examinations, including NEET-UG and CBSE board examinations, and would demand the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The application specified a protest from 10 am to 5 pm and listed Sonam Wangchuk as a participant. The accompanying undertaking committed the organisers to maintaining order, deploying volunteers, following police directions and keeping the gathering within the permitted limit of 1,000 people. Delhi Police granted permission for the June 20 demonstration, but the protest continued into June 21. The eventual turnout of thousands, at the protests which lasted over a month, was also far greater than what CJP had sought permission for. Police says Jantar Mantar can accommodate 1,000 people In its statement on X, Delhi Police said Jantar Mantar could accommodate around 1,000 people at a time. It argued that authorities needed advance information about the number of expected participants to arrange traffic diversions, emergency access and safe crowd movement. The police said Delhi's economic activity and daily life could not be brought to a halt every time a protest took place. It said the restrictions were temporary measures intended to regulate the movement of people, prevent overcrowding and protect protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area. The police also referred to Supreme Court directions issued on July 23, 2018, concerning the regulation of protests, saying the applicable guidelines had to be followed strictly. Delhi Police and central security agencies have reviewed their handling of the July protests, identifying security lapses and preparing for further demonstrations. The review included concerns about food deliveries allowing people to remain at Jantar Mantar overnight and broken pavement stones and walls that could pose security risks. The report also noted that a Supreme Court-appointed committee was examining allegations of police excesses during the July protests. Cops denied BSF permission to protest at Jantar Mantar too Meanwhile, nearly 400 former Border Security Force (BSF) cooks, water carriers and women tradesmen from various states, under the banner of the Alliance of All Ex-Paramilitary Forces, staged a peaceful protest near the BSF headquarters, seeking reinstatement in service. The alliance's general secretary, Ranbir Singh, shared a copy of a Delhi Police letter denying them permission to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 9 and 10. The letter, issued around a month earlier, cited rules against holding a hunger strike continuously for two days at Jantar Mantar and asked the organisers to cooperate with Delhi Police. “Police denied permission citing different rules for us to protest at Jantar Mantar for two days. So we held protests near the BSF headquarters today. These people were duped by cyber fraudsters who helped them get NSDC skill development certificates, which were later found to be forged. These are people who served in the BSF during Operation Sindoor but lost their jobs after the department learnt their certificates were not accredited by the NSDC. The fact is they also did not know and submitted what they got,” Singh said. What is CJP protesting against? CJP has been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. news.headline: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
news.story_lead: "I'm not going to be watching it" - JD Vance on possible livestreamed execution - Published 9 October 2026, 19:24 BST US Vice-President JD Vance has cast doubt on the Pentagon's plans to livestream a firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter. Talking with reporters, Vance expressed doubt that it would happen as planned, saying: "I don't know that that's actually going to happen". He added, that "if it's through live stream, I'm not going to be watching it".
news.full_article_text: "I'm not going to be watching it" - JD Vance on possible livestreamed execution - Published 9 October 2026, 19:24 BST US Vice-President JD Vance has cast doubt on the Pentagon's plans to livestream a firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter. Talking with reporters, Vance expressed doubt that it would happen as planned, saying: "I don't know that that's actually going to happen". He added, that "if it's through live stream, I'm not going to be watching it". Vance described the actions by former US Army major Nidal Hasan as "the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11". Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32. His execution by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years. The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute Hasan by firing squad, the first of its kind since the end of World War Two. Then on Thursday US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be livestreamed for the public. "People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," said Hegseth. The BBC has asked the White House whether Trump supported the plans. Speaking to reporters on Friday, Vance said: "I see these announcements. I don't know that that's actually going to happen." The vice-president said that Hasan was meant to treat soldiers for mental illness and other problems and "took them at their most vulnerable and gunned down these people where they lived". The announcement over the livestream plans has been met with criticism from both political parties. Republican Senator John Curtis pointed to Rome's history of a "bloody spectacle" corrupting people who watched them, warning that public executions erode civilisations "when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment". Curtis said that Hegseth's plan "risks feeding that appetite" and urged him to reconsider. "The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent," he said. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group. The US Conference of Catholic Bishops condemned the decision to publicly livestream Hasan's execution, expressing "shock and great sorrow" in a statement. The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture". Talking with reporters, Vance expressed doubt that it would happen as planned, saying: "I don't know that that's actually going to happen". Speaking to reporters on Friday, Vance said: "I see these announcements. I don't know that that's actually going to happen." The vice-president said that Hasan was meant to treat soldiers for mental illness and other problems and "took them at their most vulnerable and gunned down these people where they lived". The announcement over the livestream plans has been met with criticism from both political parties. Republican Senator John Curtis pointed to Rome's history of a "bloody spectacle" corrupting people who watched them, warning that public executions erode civilisations "when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment". Curtis said that Hegseth's plan "risks feeding that appetite" and urged him to reconsider. "The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent," he said. Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group. The US Conference of Catholic Bishops condemned the decision to publicly livestream Hasan's execution, expressing "shock and great sorrow" in a statement. The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture". news.headline: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
news.story_lead: The ICC said it would not be "deterred" by the sanctions - Published 9 October 2026, 17:06 BST The Trump administration has unveiled sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it sees as a "rogue" institution. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans. The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order.
news.full_article_text: The ICC said it would not be "deterred" by the sanctions - Published 9 October 2026, 17:06 BST The Trump administration has unveiled sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a significant acceleration of its attempt to "dismantle" what it sees as a "rogue" institution. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the measures - which include a ban on US entities making transactions with the ICC - were intended to "defend US sovereignty" and accused the court of seeking to prosecute Americans. The ICC said the measures were an assault on the rule of law and the foundations of the international legal order. The announcement came just hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law. The US has already sanctioned 17 of the ICC's judges and officials, but this move sanctions the court itself as an institution and is intended to collapse its ability to operate financially. However, the US has provided a six month grace period before some of these latest sanctions kick in, meaning member states can keep paying for its operations - a move Washington says is to allow countries time to negotiate a "solution to address" US concerns. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the US decision "a serious blow to our collective pursuit of international criminal justice, of which the ICC is a key pillar". Marco Rubio said that "either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC" The UK joined Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan and the Netherlands in reaffirming their "continued and unwavering support" for the ICC and said they "regret and strongly disagree with" the sanctions. They also praised the court's staff for their work bringing "those accused of the most serious international crimes to justice", as well as supporting victims. The ICC was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and counts 125 countries as member states. Several major countries remain outside the ICC, including the US, Russia, China, India and Israel. The Trump administration argues the ICC is run by what it calls globalists who threaten American sovereignty. It is furious over a past investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan the court has since closed and by its arrest warrants for Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The new sanctions, however, do not say that those warrants must be withdrawn before the measures can be lifted. But Rubio said Trump would not allow the ICC to prosecute Americans, adding: "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC." The US sanctions will stop US companies from providing goods or services to the ICC, such as banking or software. Rubio said Washington had delayed imposing the sanctions in the hope that the ICC and its member countries would address US concerns. He said the measures had been structured to allow other countries to negotiate a possible solution. He also called on US allies that were ICC signatories, including the UK, to "rein in" the institution. The Netherlands, which hosts the court in The Hague and is also a Nato ally of the US, faces particular pressure. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen has said the sanctions would seriously affect the court's ability to function. Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions, saying the ICC was "not a court" but a political body that threatened law-abiding democracies and "the very idea of national sovereignty". Among those awaiting trial in The Hague is Rodrigo Duterte, the former president of the Philippines The ICC said that the sanctions were aimed at disrupting its work and intimidating those who co-operate with it - but that it "will not be deterred". It called the measures "an assault on the rule of law" and said no one should be punished for serving the cause of justice, adding: "History will judge this moment." This showdown potentially marks the gravest crisis in the court's 24-year history. Rather than targeting individual ICC judges and prosecutors, the US is now sanctioning the court itself. The sanctions could ultimately see the ICC unable to try cases, meaning detainees awaiting trial or judgment could have to be released, according to Professor Ryan Goodman from the New York University School of Law. Among those awaiting trial in The Hague is Rodrigo Duterte, the former president of the Philippines. The 81-year-old is accused of the extrajudicial killing of thousands during his deadly "war on drugs" between 2011 and 2019. Others awaiting trial or with pending appeals include former senior figures accused of war crimes in Libya, Sudan and the Central African Republic. Goodman says that as a senator, Rubio was "out front" highlighting Duterte's alleged crimes. He told the BBC such a release would be "enormously damaging to the global effort towards international justice [and] towards the Philippines". "[For] the victims, it just has to be incredibly traumatic because a lot of them participate in the ICC proceedings to put themselves on the line with a hope that justice will come around," adds Goodman, a former special counsel at the US Department of Defence. Among the carve-outs announced as part of today's sanctions are "licenses" allowing the ICC to continue "services for the operation of facilities used for the detention" of Duterte and others. However, Goodman says ultimately these detainees may have to be released "as a matter of law" if the financial sanctions mean the court cannot conduct fair trials or appeals. news.story_lead: Parliamentary panel asks for a public tech strategy and a new coordination body The committee is also learnt to have recommended a separate “technology diplomacy strategy” for the MEA The parliamentary committee on external affairs has asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to prepare a public "technology vision and strategy document", saying it was surprised that India lacks a single written strategy linking technology with its foreign policy. news.full_article_text: Parliamentary panel asks for a public tech strategy and a new coordination body The committee is also learnt to have recommended a separate “technology diplomacy strategy” for the MEA The parliamentary committee on external affairs has asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to prepare a public "technology vision and strategy document", saying it was surprised that India lacks a single written strategy linking technology with its foreign policy. Calling the current approach “fragmentary, piecemeal and ad hoc”, the panel said individual successes cannot substitute for a national vision. The committee, chaired by Shashi Tharoor, recommended that the MEA work with the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and other departments to prepare the document after consulting academia, research institutions and industry. The panel said the document should outline India’s goals, priorities and the roles of different ministries. It also recommended a separate “technology diplomacy strategy” for the MEA. Both documents should be made public and reviewed periodically, it said. The committee called for a formal inter-ministerial body on technology diplomacy, chaired by the MEA and including the IT, science, space and commerce ministries, to ensure regular coordination rather than a case-by-case approach. The recommendations are part of the committee’s 17th report, adopted on September 22 and presented to the Lok Sabha Speaker on September 25. Revision of AI strategy The report said India had significant strengths in artificial intelligence (AI) but still faced gaps in computing power, data centre capacity, access to advanced chips, and private investment in large AI models. It noted that NITI Aayog’s national AI strategy was drafted before the emergence of large language models and recommended that NITI Aayog and MeitY revise it in consultation with the MEA. India has risen to third place from seventh globally on the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Tool, an interactive benchmarking suite developed by the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) to compare national AI ecosystems. However, the committee cautioned that the gap with the US and China remained substantial, calling it “a difference of kind and not only of degree”. The recommendations come as MeitY announced on Thursday that it would release a consultation paper within a month as a precursor to framing AI regulations. The paper will focus on safety, humanity, skilling, inclusivity and harm mitigation. Data centre figures unverified The committee questioned claims that India holds about 20% of the world’s data but accounts for only 3% of global data centre capacity. MeitY told the panel that neither figure was officially verified. Industry estimates, cited in the report, suggest capacity may need to rise from around 1.5 gigawatts in 2025 to 5-10 GW by 2030. The committee recommended that the MEA coordinate with MeitY and other ministries to collect and publish verified data to guide international investments and technology partnerships. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sejal Sharma I am a technology policy reporter with the National Political Bureau at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi. I cover digital policy and the intersection of technology and society, focusing mainly on what's happening in India. My beat often involves tracking platform regulation, privacy, internet curbs, and the real-world impact of digital rules, among other things. Can usually be found reading government notifications so that you don't have to. I cover three key ministries: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Ministry of Communications, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B). I am originally from New Delhi and a graduate of the Asian College of Journalism, Chennai. Over the past nine years, I have worked across television, digital and print media with The Secretariat, CNN-News18, Tiranga TV, Interesting Engineering, and now Hindustan Times. Revision of AI strategy The report said India had significant strengths in artificial intelligence (AI) but still faced gaps in computing power, data centre capacity, access to advanced chips, and private investment in large AI models. It noted that NITI Aayog’s national AI strategy was drafted before the emergence of large language models and recommended that NITI Aayog and MeitY revise it in consultation with the MEA. India has risen to third place from seventh globally on the Stanford Global AI Vibrancy Tool, an interactive benchmarking suite developed by the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) to compare national AI ecosystems. The paper will focus on safety, humanity, skilling, inclusivity and harm mitigation. news.exam_corner_topic: Supreme Court seeks Centre, states’ response on deaths of 32 tribal children in MP
news.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre, states’ response on deaths of 32 tribal children in MP
news.story_lead: Supreme Court seeks Centre, states’ response on deaths of 32 tribal children in MP The Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on compensation and measures to protect Baiga tribal children after about 32 deaths in Balaghat. The Supreme Court on Friday termed the deaths of about 32 tribal children in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat as “most unfortunate” and sought responses from the Centre and the Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh governments on providing compensation to the victims’ families and taking effective steps to protect other children suffering from severe malnutrition and a lack of drinking water facilities. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said, “What has happened is a very unfortunate thing,” as it issued notice on a petition filed by Balaghat resident Ajab Lal Lilhare.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court seeks Centre, states’ response on deaths of 32 tribal children in MP The Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh on compensation and measures to protect Baiga tribal children after about 32 deaths in Balaghat. The Supreme Court on Friday termed the deaths of about 32 tribal children in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat as “most unfortunate” and sought responses from the Centre and the Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh governments on providing compensation to the victims’ families and taking effective steps to protect other children suffering from severe malnutrition and a lack of drinking water facilities. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said, “What has happened is a very unfortunate thing,” as it issued notice on a petition filed by Balaghat resident Ajab Lal Lilhare. While the bench was initially inclined to refer the matter to the Madhya Pradesh High Court, advocate Varun Thakur, who argued the petition, submitted that the problem concerned children of the Baiga tribe, which has a presence in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh due to the states’ common border. He stated that despite the petitioner submitting written representations to the authorities and elected representatives of the area, the early warnings were ignored, leading to the tragedy. The petition states that since January 2026, when the Balaghat-Seoni MP and local authorities were first informed of the worsening health situation among children, the authorities in Madhya Pradesh remained in a “bureaucratic slumber” until the first death occurred after August. The cause of death, following visits by epidemiological teams, was confirmed to be measles-rubella, the petition said. The virus preys lethally on children whose immune systems are compromised by long-term protein-calorie malnutrition and a severe lack of vitamin A supplementation, it said. In January, a social worker had alerted the local authorities that a severe, undiagnosed paediatric epidemic was rapidly spreading among Baiga children in Balaghat. The district has no doctors, diagnostic facilities or essential medicines in its forest belt. Sporadic health camps organised in January and February this year were prematurely abandoned without active surveillance, serological testing or vital cold-chain immunisation drives, the petition said. The local Anganwadi centres did not provide daily supplementary nutritional meals to tribal infants, and ration supplies for joint families were restricted to single-member allocations. This caused systemic starvation, the petition stated, seeking a response from the state authorities over their failure to act in time and prevent the deaths. The petition sought a direction from the court to declare the Baihar-Birsa block region of Balaghat district “epidemic prone” under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897. It also sought compensation for the victims’ families, along with a supply of 10 litres of drinking water per person per day and nutritious food. Instead of rectifying their mistakes, the petition said, following reports of the deaths, the district administration issued a blanket gag order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), penalising citizens and grassroots whistleblowers for photographing, recording or publishing administrative failures in public health institutions. The petition raised concerns about the surviving children in the Balaghat area and sought consolidated, time-bound directions and structural changes to ensure transparency in reporting deaths, immunisation drives, nutrition delivery and compensation to affected families. The Baiga tribe is one of India’s most ancient communities. It is geographically isolated and characterised by low literacy rates and stagnant demographic growth, making its members extremely vulnerable. The nearest community health centre to Balaghat is almost 40 kilometres away, and even this centre lacks effective nursing care and emergency referral transport, the petition states. This has forced the tribal population to rely on unqualified practitioners, further threatening their existence, it added.

news.headline: DMRC revises order after Supreme Court rap, 45 Delhi Metro stations to remain affected
news.story_lead: DMRC revises order after Supreme Court rap, 45 Delhi Metro stations to remain affected The Supreme Court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to lift blanket restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of CJP's protests in Delhi on Saturday. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) revised its order on the closure of 45 metro stations following a rap from the Supreme Court. The top court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to lift blanket restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of CJP's protests in Delhi on Saturday.
news.full_article_text: DMRC revises order after Supreme Court rap, 45 Delhi Metro stations to remain affected The Supreme Court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to lift blanket restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of CJP's protests in Delhi on Saturday. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) revised its order on the closure of 45 metro stations following a rap from the Supreme Court. The top court directed the Centre and Delhi Police to lift blanket restrictions on metro and railway services ahead of CJP's protests in Delhi on Saturday. DMRC reduced the number of metro stations affected by security restrictions ahead of the CJP protest from 57 to 45. “Entry and exit at the 45 stations will remain closed from 9 pm on October 9 to 6 pm on October 10 due to security reasons. This is in partial modification of the update shared earlier about the closure of Metro stations,” it posted on X. Also Read | Full list of 45 Delhi Metro stations to have restricted entry during CJP's Jantar Mantar protest tomorrow Entry and exit will remain closed at the following 45 Delhi metro stations on October 10 including: Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Lok Kalyan Marg, Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Seva Teerth, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, ITO, Delhi Gate, Khan Market, Ramakrishna Ashram Marg, Jhandewalan, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, Shivaji Stadium, Dilli Haat-INA, Hauz Khas, Jor Bagh, Lajpat Nagar, Jangpura, Ashram, Jamia Millia Islamia, Chawri Bazar, Jama Masjid, Karol Bagh, Rajendra Place, Vishwavidyalaya, Kashmere Gate, Inderlok, Guru Tegh Bahadur Nagar, Netaji Subhash Place, Azadpur, Jahangirpuri, Haiderpur Badli Mor, Majlis Park, Seelampur, Maujpur-Babarpur, Jafrabad, Welcome, Yamuna Vihar, Khajuri Khas, Shahdara and Rithala. Security agencies will review the situation, and further updates will be shared accordingly. Interchange facilities will remain available at all the affected stations, except the New Delhi Metro station. The Supreme Court made it clear that security measures cannot amount to a complete prohibition on public transport and inconvenience millions of ordinary residents. Earlier in the day, the DMRC announced that entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations will remain closed from 9pm onwards on October 9. Deep Dive A bench, comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said that authorities could regulate the movement of trains to prevent unlawful gatherings but could not bring the entire system to a halt, stressing that the right of Delhi’s residents to access public facilities and move freely also required protection. “Stopping something and regulating are two different concepts. One can regulate but it is completely different to put a halt on everything…you cannot stop everything,” observed the bench. “You will not use a hammer to kill a fly,” remarked the court, explaining that the authorities must adopt measures commensurate with the situation rather than impose sweeping restrictions. The court was told that railway services had also been disrupted ahead of the demonstration. Indian Railways cancelled mail and express trains scheduled to arrive at or depart from New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10, citing anticipated severe road congestion around the stations. The cancellations affected long-distance services, including the Howrah-New Delhi and Sealdah-New Delhi Rajdhani Express trains. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times.
